claims.statement: AEG Solar directs private customers to their installer and asks installer-channel claimants for model, serial number, purchase reference, defect description, and pictures.
Fronius states that free inverter warranty cover depends on portal registration within a defined period, illustrating that preventive registration timing can affect later recovery.

contrary_evidence: Manufacturer and distributor portals already perform the formal claim intake, so the value must come from cross-OEM recovery and labour saved rather than merely digitising a form.
Some warranty terms exclude travel, labour, consequential loss, or claims by intermediaries, limiting recoverable value.

economics.acquisition_route: Prove recovered value on a bounded family-business backlog, then sell through wholesalers and installer service communities
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A plausible 5-7 year route would require several thousand installer accounts across multiple countries, an average of roughly 2,000-3,000 PLN annual gross profit per account, and expansion into preventive registration or warranty analytics while the founder retains substantial equity
economics.founder_time: Approximately 10-14 hours per week after a part-time warranty specialist handles manufacturer follow-up
economics.gross_margin_basis: Automation and pooled specialist handling of repetitive claims, net of technician review, shipping coordination, and disputed-value appraisal
economics.payback: One recovered inverter, heat-pump component, or labour allowance may cover several months of fees; actual recovery frequency and value require sample audits
economics.pricing: 299-999 PLN per installer per month plus 8-15% of cash, credit, labour allowance, or replacement value actually recovered
economics.retention_or_repeat: Recurring installed-base failures, new equipment registrations, and multiple OEM programmes create ongoing use

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A serial-level map of required evidence, failure modes, response times, exclusions, and realised recovery by OEM could improve claim routing and preventive registration
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish and Central European solar, storage, and heat-pump installers and O&M firms
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Start with the family company's installed base, then partner with component wholesalers, O&M associations, insurer brokers, and installer ERP vendors
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Cross-OEM warranty rules, evidence intake, AI-assisted dossier preparation, status chasing, and a settlement receipt; charge subscription plus 8-15% of measurable recovered value
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The installer pays a modest monthly platform fee and a percentage when an OEM or distributor authorises a replacement, service credit, or cash reimbursement
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Installed equipment fails or underperforms and recovery depends on a vendor-specific chain of registration, proof, diagnosis, shipping, and reimbursement conditions

founder_fit: The founder can obtain de-identified workflow observations from a family renewable installer before building broadly
Document extraction, classification, and exception analytics fit AI and data-science strengths
The service can be delivered asynchronously with limited public visibility
risks: OEM terms may prohibit assignment or third-party representation
Recovered replacement value may be hard to price consistently for a success fee
Manufacturers could deny claims for installation errors and damage installer relationships
Manual follow-up could turn the business into a low-margin agency

structure.commercial_archetype: Subscription plus success-fee warranty claims administrator
structure.control_point: A limited claims mandate and the canonical equipment dossier linking serial number, owner, installer, commissioning, purchase, diagnosis, and recovery outcome
structure.critical_dependency: OEMs and distributors must accept authorised third-party submissions and expose a clearly measurable recovery outcome

thesis: Small photovoltaic, battery, and heat-pump installers could outsource fragmented manufacturer and distributor warranty administration to a software-assisted claims desk. The service would assemble serial, invoice, commissioning, error-code, and photo evidence, pursue the authorised channel, and charge for successful replacement, credit, or cash recovery rather than asking installers to master each OEM process.
title: Renewable Warranty Recovery Desk
uncertainties: Claim frequency and unrecovered value per typical installer installed base
Whether distributors will share portal access or accept structured dossiers
How often labour and travel costs, rather than equipment value, are the true loss
Whether a common equipment passport can span enough OEMs without excessive maintenance
